title: Using the System Text Editor

children: You can use the System Text Editor to edit SCALE resource values. This is especially helpful if you want to add a custom graphic or change a term used on system windows. There are four types of resource files that you can modify: text, messages, images, and help. Also, there is one of these resource files for each language that you support. For example, if you support English and Spanish: there is an English text resource file and a Spanish text resource file. For detailed descriptions of each type of resource file, see the descriptions below. The System Text Editor also includes two tools (Translation Wizard and Localize Reports) to assist you with translation management.

System 
 Text Editor Detail Window Fields
The following is discussed in this topic:

Text: This resource file 
 consists of text labels that appear throughout the system, such as field 
 names or menu options. Any change that you make to a value here is applied 
 through the entire system. For example, if you change the word File to 
 Start, all instances of the word File in the system's menus, toolbars 
 and fields are changed to Start. Of course, phrases that include the word 
 changed are not impacted.

Messages: This resource 
 file contains all error messages and warnings generated by the system. 
 These messages are tied to processes, not to particular screens. This 
 allows them to be reused throughout the system on multiple screens.

Images: This resource file 
 contains all graphic images used in the system, such as browser icons. 
 If you want to add a new graphic to the system, you must first add it 
 to the resourceImage directory on your server. It is located in a system 
 directory and contains all graphics available to the system. Currently, 
 the system supports the following graphic file types: .bmp and .gif

Help: This resource file 
 contains the names/paths of help topics associated with system windows. 
 Do not change a help name/path without discussing possible ramifications 
 with your system consultant.

You can press the key combination CTRL+R 
 on any SCALE window, and the system will display the resource keys for all 
 the fields on the current window. Note that if you press this sequence 
 again, you can toggle back on the field's actual display name.
Values that have had custom text provided for them are colored yellow.

You can use the System Text Editor Window to edit values in a resource 
 group. This is especially helpful if you want to replace a default word 
 with one that reflects your business or if you want to add your own graphics 
 to the system.

By default all users will have access to delete, edit and create resources from the System Text Editor.  The system administrator can create User, Group or System security to restrict users from modifying resources.
In web.configuration, Text Localization is the new name for this functionality. You can also delete and create custom resource keys based on base resource keys.
Access the System Text Editor Window.

Use the Language and Group Fields to identify which resource group contains 
 the values that you want to modify.

Use the Additional 
 Criteria Fields to narrow your search for records. The system will 
 filter through the resource group's records and display only those that 
 meet this criteria. You can use any combination of these fields.

Use the Key Field if you know the actual key name that 
 you want to access. The key links the text, message, or image to the base 
 code in the system.
The Screen Field is reserved for future use.

Use the Search Text Field 
 if you know the name, or part of the name, of the value that you want 
 to access. When you provide text here, the system displays all instances 
 of this text in the record list. If you want to change all instances of 
 this value, provide the replacement value in the Replace Text Field.

Use the Custom Text Only Checkbox if you only want to search for custom 
 values. If you select this checkbox and provide a value in the Replace 
 Text Field, the system will only replace custom values; base values will 
 not be impacted.

Use the Case Sensitive Checkbox 
 if you want the system to consider case when searching for values. When 
 its selected, the system will only display those values with the same 
 case as the value you defined in the Search Text Field.

Use the Search Text and Replace 
 Text Fields to subset a 
 search for a specific text string. When you enter a value in the Search 
 Text Field, the system will search for your data in the "Base Text" 
 column of the resource group (see the graphic below). When you enter a 
 value in the Replace Text Field, the system will replace the Search Text 
 Field value with the data you provide in this field.

Note: You 
 cannot use the Replace Option if the Group is Images.

Select the Search and Replace Button. 
 Did you provide a replacement value in the Replace Text Field?

If you used the Replace Text 
 Field, the system will display all values that met your search 
 in the record list. Your replacement value will appear in the Custom Value 
 Column. The original value appears in the Base Value Column. You can change 
 any of the values in the Custom Text Column, or remove them. This is especially 
 helpful if you want the custom value to apply to most keys in the system, 
 but want to further modify a few specific keys.

If you did 
 not use the Replace Text Field, the system will display all values 
 that meet your criteria in the Base Value Column. Any existing custom 
 values are displayed in the Custom Value Column. Use the Base Value Column 
 to locate the value you want to change. In the corresponding Custom Value 
 Column, provide the new value that will replace this base value. If the 
 Group is Images, the Custom Value Column is a pull-down menu that you 
 can select the graphic from.

If you are changing a time and/or date entry, it will include an 
 ampersand (&) in the base value. You can move the ampersand in the 
 custom value, but do not remove it! The system reads ampersands and replaces 
 them with the appropriate time and/or date calculation.

Select Apply. The system will display a message verifying that you want to commit this change to the database. Select Yes. The system will commit this change to the database. This change will impact the system's screens and windows as soon as the application is closed and reopened.  An IISRESET is required to see changes in browser-based or WPF screens. The Text Last Updated phrase, at the top of the screen, will change to the current date and time.
Repeat steps 1 – 4 to search and replace resource values for other languages or groups.
WARNING: If you cannot see changes made in the System Text Editor after exiting and re-entering the system, a shutdown of the system package(s) in Component Services may be required.

NOTE FOR BROWSER-RELATED SETTINGS: When you change a browser-related (TPM and RF) or WPF (Desktop and Dock Manager UI) resource file value, this new value will not take effect until the Windows IISRESET command is executed. This command completely shuts down and restarts IIS, so it should be performed when no one is using the TPM, RF or WPF screens.

A new release of the system will have 
 NO impact on a custom value. However, custom values are not automatically 
 applied to new keys in this release.

You cannot modify a base value's field length or its decimal position. 
 Instead, you will create a custom value that is exactly the same as the 
 base value. Then, you can change this custom value's field length and/or 
 decimal position. See the topic

topic for more information on this 
 subject.

Use the Language 
 and Group Fields to identify which resource group contains the values 
 that you want to modify.

Use the Search 
 Fields to locate the base value that you want to modify. See the 
 procedures for "Editing Resource Group Values," (Step 2) for 
 more information on the search fields.

Right click on 
 the appropriate base value. Select Open Custom Value. The system 
 will display all of the base values for this new custom value. You can 
 change any of the following fields: Custom Text, Field Length, and Decimal 
 Position.

Apply these changes. 
 Generate a new Resource Group. Close and Reopen the system. See the procedures 
 for "Editing Resource Group Values" (Steps 4-6) for more information 
 about these procedures.

When you access 
 the value in the system, its field length and/or decimal position 
 will reflect the changes that you made to the custom text.

You can change the following characteristics for a custom value: field 
 length and decimal position. You can also create a new custom text value.

Use the Language 
 and Group Fields to identify which resource group contains the values 
 that you want to modify.

Use the Search 
 Fields to locate the base value that you want to modify. See the 
 procedures for "Editing Resource Group Values" (Step 2) for more 
 information on the search fields.

Press the Search 
 Button. The system will display the results in the record list.

To edit a value, 
 right click on the appropriate custom text value, and choose the "Open 
 Custom Value" option. The system will display all of the base values 
 for this new custom value. You can change any of the following fields: 
 Custom Text, Field Length, and Decimal Position.

To create a new value, right click on a custom text value and 
 choose the "New Custom Value" option. The system will display 
 the a window where you can define the specifics of your new custom text 
 value. Press OK when finished.
Click Apply to commit the changes. Close and Reopen the system. See the procedures for "Editing Resource File Values" (Steps 4-6) for more information about these procedures.

When you access the value in the system, its field 
 length and/or decimal position will reflect the changes that you made 
 to the custom text.

If you edit or translate a paperwork document field in the System Text 
 Editor, you will need to "localize" the resource values of these 
 documents, in order for your changes to actually appear on the document. This needs to be done for SQL Server Reporting Services (SSRS). For more information on this process, see the topic

 Editable Field Decimal Positions topic for more information on this 
 subject.

        

            
Use the Language 
 and Group Fields to identify which resource group contains the values 
 that you want to modify.





            
Use the Search 
 Fields to locate the base value that you want to modify. See the 
 procedures for "Editing Resource Group Values," (Step 2) for 
 more information on the search fields.





            
Right click on 
 the appropriate base value. Select Open Custom Value. The system 
 will display all of the base values for this new custom value. You can 
 change any of the following fields: Custom Text, Field Length, and Decimal 
 Position.





            
Apply these changes. 
 Generate a new Resource Group. Close and Reopen the system. See the procedures 
 for "Editing Resource Group Values" (Steps 4-6) for more information 
 about these procedures.





            
When you access 
 the value in the system, its field length and/or decimal position 
 will reflect the changes that you made to the custom text.

        

        
 

        
 

        

 Editing/Creating a Custom Text Value...

        
You can change the following characteristics for a custom value: field 
 length and decimal position. You can also create a new custom text value.

        

            
Use the Language 
 and Group Fields to identify which resource group contains the values 
 that you want to modify.





            
Use the Search 
 Fields to locate the base value that you want to modify. See the 
 procedures for "Editing Resource Group Values" (Step 2) for more 
 information on the search fields.





            
Press the Search 
 Button. The system will display the results in the record list.





            
To edit a value, 
 right click on the appropriate custom text value, and choose the "Open 
 Custom Value" option. The system will display all of the base values 
 for this new custom value. You can change any of the following fields: 
 Custom Text, Field Length, and Decimal Position.



To create a new value, right click on a custom text value and 
 choose the "New Custom Value" option. The system will display 
 the a window where you can define the specifics of your new custom text 
 value. Press OK when finished.





            
Click Apply to commit the changes. Close and Reopen the system. See the procedures for "Editing Resource File Values" (Steps 4-6) for more information about these procedures.





            
When you access the value in the system, its field 
 length and/or decimal position will reflect the changes that you made 
 to the custom text.

        

        
 

        
 

        

 Localizing Reports...

        
 

        
If you edit or translate a paperwork document field in the System Text 
 Editor, you will need to "localize" the resource values of these 
 documents, in order for your changes to actually appear on the document. This needs to be done for SQL Server Reporting Services (SSRS). For more information on this process, see the topic Localizing Values On Paperwork Documents.
